      "observations": [
        "All 15 owned paths and full changed bodies were read: author-owned parser/extractor/naming/token generation plus generated Entity, DirectoryObject, MailboxSettings, module list and all 793 diff lines of User. Generated output was studied as an integration contract, not excluded by size or treated as handwritten style authority.",
        "The initial standalone generator is a separate Cargo workspace. main reads caller-supplied YAML and an output crate path, parses schemas, filters four SUPPORTED_TYPES, extracts Graph properties, then emits Rust files and a sorted module list. It does not download a schema, build every Graph path or run itself during the ordinary crate build. The README gives a manifest-based cargo command; the actual package remains graph_tb_extract even though directory/disclosure prose uses ms_graph_tb_extract.",
        "The parser models refs and object metadata including nullable, arrays and allOf/oneOf/anyOf. Extraction skips navigation and @odata properties, follows only supported custom types and builds typed properties independently of descriptions. Nested arrays and binary/base64 conversion have todo branches; unsupported objects and numeric formats can panic; unsupported refs are logged/skipped. Decimal maps to f64 with an explicit lossiness comment. This is selected schema translation, not complete OpenAPI validation.",
        "Token emission sorts imports, selection variants and accessor functions, constructs PascalCase types/variants and snake_case functions, and emits provenance doc attributes plus overwrite markers. The old writer uses File::create per output file and assumes src/types already exists, so failure is not an atomic tree replacement. No deterministic-byte regeneration or full compiler coverage is established merely by sorting output names.",
        "Generated accessors retain the earlier raw Cow-map missing/null/type-error contract and now include numeric conversion, custom MailboxSettings borrowing and more User properties. Nullable arrays are supported only under the generator's explicit assumption that their elements are nonnull. The four-type preview and current typed optional-field representation are distinct; earlier exact property-contract knowledge is reused rather than duplicated.",
        "The generated usage_location description says Not nullable, while its return type is Result<Option<&str>, Error> and its explicit JSON-null branch returns Ok(None). Description prose is copied separately from the parsed nullable flag. This is a precise documentation/type mismatch; the unseen upstream schema and no runtime result cannot decide which side should change.",
        "No unit tests are introduced in the generator/output changes. The six new naming assert calls have nonempty diagnostic messages for empty/keyword identifiers; missing should alone is not a defect. YAML expect messages are nonempty. Existing crate unit tests belong to 4334 and are not recredited as generator tests. No golden-output, null-element, unsupported-schema, naming, compile or regeneration case was executed.",
        "The author-owned modules have useful purpose and conversion-order comments. map_openapi_schema_to_rust nests primitive/array/composition cases; a named array-mapping helper could separate nested-array rejection from primitive mapping as a scoped readability suggestion. Do not manually reflow generated doc attributes or treat their dense blank-line layout as a global exception; generator source and output have separate roles.",
        "Fixed accepted source is later work: support lists are external object/enum/path files, generation covers both paths and types with module hierarchy, output writers create parent directories, and generated structs are typed. The current comm Python wrapper verifies a pinned schema URL/digest before deleting/recreating output directories, then runs locked cargo generation, formatting, Clippy fixes and formatting again. These later controls are not attributed to this first generator landing, and none were run here.",
        "Complete Bug 1995802 is reused with its exact original C collector ID and scope, already reconciled for 4334; four source phases and combined Try locator remain distinct. Full D275648 creation-to-final timeline and all 18 actual inline bodies were read, including five older bodies from pinned 1169790 and current/outdated rows linked to 1171636/1174494. There are no summary or test-plan edits.",
        "The reviewer asks for module-flow documentation and public-type/function explanations; the author explains parse OpenAPI, extract Graph information, emit Rust, with main handling I/O. Landed module headers and OaSchema/RustType/GraphType docs provide those roles. The author removes one vestigial private-helper comment instead of widening visibility. This is actual scoped response, not a rule to document every private symbol.",
        "The exact regeneration-command request and upstream-fork question remain marked Not Done in rows, but source adds the manifest-based README command and author/reviewer explicitly agree to use upstream for now. The external YAML was deliberately not vendored. Later pinned-download/build integration was proposed for the future, not implemented by this initial landing; current later comm wrapper was checked separately.",
        "The Clippy version-guard idea is explicitly deferred because the author reports no known differing outputs in practice; it is not an adopted guard or a measured reproducibility result. The optional error-library suggestion is corrected from thiserror to anyhow and remains nonblocking; the owned generator still uses Box<dyn std::error::Error>. Approval/build/landing events do not prove generation or test results."
